title: Failover: add burn-rate alert rules + annotations for regional impairment (paging routing)
author: Sergio Costa
description: Summary: Adds burn-rate alert rules (fast + slow) for regional impairment detection and wires them into paging routing so on-call gets a single, actionable page per region/product when we are actually burning multi-region availability SLO. This is intended to replace the current mix of threshold alerts and ad-hoc dashboards that have been noisy in staging. Details: (1) New burn-rate alerts for Hosted API and Dedicated ingress using multi-window evaluation (5m/1h fast-burn + 30m/6h slow-burn) over request success (5xx + timeouts) and tail latency SLOs; (2) Reachability corroboration alerts (perf-canary cross-region probes + public edge checks) to distinguish “region is impaired” vs “local service issue”; (3) Alert annotations standardized for failover workflows: include dashboard links, runbook link, suggested next steps (check Region Health, run failover-controller dry-run /simulate, validate capacity headroom), and a short “why we think this is real” evidence string; (4) Paging routing integration: fast-burn pages to SRE primary (service: sre-failover) with product-specific routing (hosted-vs-dedicated) and warnings to #eng-sre-alerts; (5) Inhibition/grouping rules to reduce duplicate pages (e.g., suppress latency-only pages when reachability + error burn is already paging for the same region). Guardrails: Avoids high-cardinality labels (no tenant_id / model_id); groups by {product, region, route_class, tier} only. All rules are promtool-tested and include alert rule linting in CI. Rollout: Landed behind alert bundle version v2026.01.12; will be enabled in staging first, then prod during game-day go/no-go checklist. References: ADR-042 signal hierarchy (reachability > error burn > latency burn > capacity) and ENG-2418 acceptance criteria for “fast detection without paging noise.”

review_conversation: Allison Grant: Please confirm we are not paging on latency-only unless we have corroboration or SLO burn; staging has been too noisy. Also add direct links in annotations to the Failover Signals dashboard and the failover controller dry-run docs.

Sergio Costa (author): Updated. Latency paging now requires either (a) concurrent elevated 5xx burn OR (b) reachability degradation from perf-canary. Latency-only remains warning-level with a longer hold. Added dashboard + runbook links to all severity=page alerts.

Miles Thornton: For signal hierarchy alignment: can we encode “reachability first” in the alert names/labels so the controller can consume them deterministically later? Also make sure we group by region to avoid 10 pages for the same event.

Sergio Costa (author): Added label trigger_source=reachability|error_burn|latency_burn and standardized alertname prefix FailoverRegionImpairment*. Grouping keys updated to {product, region, tier} and route_class where applicable. Inhibitions now suppress downstream symptom alerts when reachability+error burn is firing for the same region.

Tomáš Novák: On-call readability: annotations should include a one-line recommended action and the exact query to validate quickly. Also add a note about silencing policy flips-related alerts during a planned game day.

Sergio Costa (author): Added “recommended_action” + “validation_query” annotations (short) and a doc note on planned-test silences. Kept queries generic (no tenant/model labels) to avoid copy-paste footguns.

Devon Price: Paging routing: make sure the PD service is correct (sre-failover) and that warnings go to #eng-sre-alerts, not #incidents. Also add an explicit annotation for incident-bot summary compatibility (it scrapes a few fields).
Sergio Costa (author): Routing updated; warnings now to #eng-sre-alerts. Added annotation incident_bot_summary_fields=product,region,tier,trigger_source to match the incident-bot parser we discussed.
Victor Alvarez: Reachability: are we using both perf-canary and edge checks? Some provider blips show up as one but not the other.

Sergio Costa (author): Yes—reachability burn pages require >=2 of (perf-canary, edge HTTP, control-plane heartbeat) for 2m, otherwise warning-only. Added comments in the rule file explaining the quorum logic.
Allison Grant: Approved (ship it). Please open a follow-up for tuning after the first prod game day once we have real data.
Sergio Costa (author): Done—will track tuning in ENG-2426 post-gameday action items.
deployment_notes: Staging: enable alert bundle v2026.01.12 in us-east + eu-west only; verify grouping/paging with synthetic burn test. Prod: keep severity=page routing disabled until game-day go/no-go; then enable for Hosted API first (tier=prod, route_class=default) with a 30m monitoring window before expanding to Dedicated.
release_notes: On-call: New regional impairment burn-rate pages are now actionable (single page per region/product) with standardized annotations linking to dashboards/runbooks and explicit next steps for failover validation.
